title: Residual phUSD delta silently dropped in _settleResidualDelta causes ClaimArbitrage DoS
description: _settleResidualDelta(phUSD) silently returns at line 364 when no stableToUSDCPool[phUSD] is configured and phUSD != sUSDS. If any residual negative phUSD delta exists from the pump/unwind cycle (which is expected due to AMM fee asymmetry and tick rounding), it remains unsettled. The Uniswap V4 PoolManager enforces that all deltas must be zero when unlock returns, so it reverts the entire execute() transaction. This renders ClaimArbitrage non-functional for any scenario producing even 1 wei of residual phUSD delta.
impact: ClaimArbitrage becomes permanently DoSed whenever the pump/unwind produces a residual phUSD delta (expected behavior due to AMM rounding). The silent return masks the root cause. Yield distribution through ClaimArbitrage is blocked.
attackPath: 1. Any user calls ClaimArbitrage.execute() with valid parameters
2. Step 1 (pump): swap sUSDS → phUSD, producing pumpDelta
3. Step 4 (unwind): sell back the phUSD received from pump
4. Due to AMM fee asymmetry, a small residual negative phUSD delta remains
7. phUSD != sUSDS, so the function silently returns at line 364
8. PoolManager detects nonzero delta and reverts with CurrencyNotSettled()
recommendation: Either configure stableToUSDCPool[phUSD] to a phUSD/USDC pool, add a fallback settlement through phUSD_sUSDS_pool, or at minimum replace the silent return with a descriptive revert so the failure mode is diagnosable.
